title: Claims Manual: Rental Reimbursement Coverage Across Several Losses and Vehicles
content:
Under Rental Reimbursement Coverage, when the named insured has several covered vehicles or several losses, rental is evaluated loss by loss and vehicle by vehicle. Each covered loss is capped separately, and only one rental is paid at a time for one loss. Benefits on one claim never use another claim's remaining maximum.

## The rule taken apart

- **Unit of evaluation:** the covered loss, on its own vehicle — never the named insured's losses taken together.
- **Caps:** each covered loss is measured against its own maximum for one covered loss and its own most rental days, as the package schedule sets them.
- **One rental at a time:** for one loss, only one rental is paid at a time.
- **No borrowing:** what remains of one claim's maximum is not available to another claim.
- **Record used:** when a rental is authorized, the authorizations already recorded under the same claim number are what the test reads; the company's records, not the customer's statement, decide it.

## Basis questions answered

**Two vehicles of the same named insured are damaged in separate covered losses. Is one maximum shared?** No. Each covered loss is capped separately, so each claim has its own maximum and its own days.

**One claim has used most of its maximum while another claim on a second vehicle has used little. May the first claim draw on the second's remainder?** No. Benefits on one claim never use another claim's remaining maximum.

**May two rental vehicles be paid at once for the same loss?** No. Only one rental is paid at a time for one loss.

## Hypothetical illustration

A named insured on the Cardinal Point Rental Reimbursement $30/$900 package has two covered claims, A and B, on two vehicles. Claim A has hypothetical paid benefits of USD 850.00; claim B has USD 120.00. Claim A is measured against its own USD 900.00 maximum, so USD 50.00 of its maximum remains; the USD 780.00 remaining on claim B is not available to claim A.
